reports.title: LOWE’S REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 SALES AND EARNINGS RESULTS

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook
section: •Comparable sales expected to be up approximately +0.5% compared to prior year (previously flat)
•Operating income as a percentage of sales (operating margin) of approximately 11.1% (previously 11.2%)
•Adjusted1 operating income as a percentage of sales (adjusted operating margin) of approximately 11.5%
•Net interest expense of approximately $1.5 billion (previously $1.6 billion)
•Adjusted1 diluted earnings per share of approximately $12.25

A conference call to discuss third quarter 2026 operating results is scheduled for today, Wednesday, November 18, at 9 a.m. ET. The conference call will be available by webcast and can be accessed by visiting Lowe’s website at ir.lowes.com and clicking on Lowe’s Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call Webcast. Supplemental slides will be available prior to the start of the conference call. A replay of the call will be archived at ir.lowes.com.

desk.headline: Sales up 9.3% to $22.8bn, beat; full-year sales outlook raised to $92.5bn, margin outlook trimmed
results: Sales rose 9.3% to $22.8bn; comparable sales were up 1.8%, helped by a 17.4% jump in online sales and growth in Pro and home services.
Both GAAP EPS ($2.98) and adjusted EPS ($3.10, up 1.3%) include a $0.34 boost from about $250m of IEEPA tariff refunds.
Gross margin fell 124bp to 32.9% and adjusted operating margin slipped to 11.7% from 12.4%.
Average ticket rose 3.5% while comparable transactions fell 1.7%; 7 of 13 product categories had positive comps.
Paid $701m in dividends ($1.25 a share, up from $1.20); quarter-end cash was $3.4bn.

guidance.summary: Lowe's lifted its 2026 sales target to about $92.5bn (from $92.0bn) and now sees comps up about 0.5% (from flat), but trimmed its margin outlook; EPS targets were left at about $11.75 GAAP and $12.25 adjusted.

points: About a third of the tariff refund was put back into prices and service in Q3; the rest goes into promotions, loyalty and fulfilment in Q4, leaving it roughly neutral for the year.
The margin trim was blamed on that reinvestment, diesel near $6 a gallon and a shift towards lower-margin appliances and outdoor power equipment.
Q4 comps are expected to be slightly positive, with January facing a tough comparison against last year's storm-related sales.
Smaller Pro customers drove growth, home services grew for a 10th straight quarter, and about half of online orders are filled from stores.
Adjusted debt is about 3.0 times EBITDA; the aim is 2.75 times in 2027, with small FBM acquisitions funded from cash.
call.source: Q3 2026 call transcript — Investing.com, 18 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (19 Aug 2026)

watch: Whether Q4 comps stay positive against the January storm comparison.
How much of the tariff refund gets reinvested and what that does to Q4 margins as fuel costs stay high.
Fiscal 2027 targets at the December analyst and investor conference.
